# Reflex Test
::: {.task-subtitle}
Measuring reaction time through the classic ruler catch task
:::
:::

## Introduction

In this task, you caught a falling **30cm ruler** 5 times. The distance you caught it at (in cm) reflects your **reaction time**. Values greater than 30cm indicate a missed catch.

**Physics refresher**: The ruler falls due to gravity. Using the equation:

$$d = \frac{1}{2}gt^2$$

We can convert distance (d) to reaction time (t):

$$t = \sqrt{\frac{2d}{g}}$$

Where g = 980 cm/s²

::: {.key-finding}
#### Key Finding
The average reaction time was approximately **175ms**, with clear evidence of a **learning effect** - people got faster with practice!
:::

## Load the Data

```{webr-r}

# Clear learning effect visible across trials

reflex <- tibble::tribble(

cat("N =", nrow(reflex), "participants\n")
cat("Handedness:", sum(reflex$hand == "Right"), "right,", sum(reflex$hand == "Left"), "left\n\n")
head(reflex)
```

## Clean the Data

The ruler was 30cm long, so any values > 30cm represent missed catches. Let's clean these:

```{webr-r}
# Cap any values > 30 at 30 (or set to NA for missed catches)
reflex <- reflex |>
  mutate(across(starts_with("t"), ~ if_else(.x > 30, NA_real_, .x)))

# Check for any cleaned values
cat("Rows with missing values after cleaning:",
    sum(!complete.cases(reflex)), "\n")
```

## Convert to Long Format

For analysis, we need the data in "long" format (one row per trial):

```{webr-r}
reflex_long <- reflex |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("t"),
    names_to = "trial",
    values_to = "distance_cm"
  ) |>
  mutate(trial = as.numeric(str_extract(trial, "\\d+")))

head(reflex_long)
```

## Calculate Reaction Time

Let's convert distance to reaction time in milliseconds:

```{webr-r}
# Add reaction time calculation
reflex_long <- reflex_long |>
  mutate(
    # RT in seconds = sqrt(2 * distance_cm / 980)
    rt_seconds = sqrt(2 * distance_cm / 980),
    # Convert to milliseconds
    rt_ms = rt_seconds * 1000
  )

# Summary by trial
reflex_long |>
  group_by(trial) |>
  summarise(
    mean_distance = mean(distance_cm),
    mean_rt_ms = mean(rt_ms),
    sd_rt_ms = sd(rt_ms)
  )
```

## Visualise Performance

```{webr-r}
ggplot(reflex_long, aes(x = factor(trial), y = distance_cm)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "#e74c3c", alpha = 0.7, outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.1, alpha = 0.6, size = 2, color = "#275882") +
  labs(
    x = "Trial",
    y = "Distance Caught (cm)",
    title = "Reaction Time Performance",
    subtitle = "Lower distance = Faster reactions"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(color = "#275882", face = "bold"),
    axis.title = element_text(color = "#275882")
  )
```

## Learning Effect

Do people get faster with practice?

```{webr-r}
# Calculate means per trial
trial_means <- reflex_long |>
  group_by(trial) |>
  summarise(
    mean_dist = mean(distance_cm),
    se = sd(distance_cm) / sqrt(n())
  )

ggplot(trial_means, aes(x = trial, y = mean_dist)) +
  geom_line(color = "#e74c3c", linewidth = 1.5) +
  geom_point(color = "#e74c3c", size = 4) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = mean_dist - se, ymax = mean_dist + se),
              alpha = 0.2, fill = "#e74c3c") +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = mean_dist - se, ymax = mean_dist + se),
    width = 0.2, color = "#e74c3c"
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Trial",
    y = "Mean Distance (cm)",
    title = "Learning Curve",
    subtitle = "Does performance improve with practice?"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(color = "#275882", face = "bold"),
    axis.title = element_text(color = "#275882")
  )
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## What Does This Show?

The **downward trend** indicates a **learning effect**:

- **Trial 1**: Participants are warming up, getting used to the task
- **Trials 2-3**: Rapid improvement as they learn the timing
- **Trials 4-5**: Performance plateaus near their optimal reaction time

This demonstrates **motor learning** and the importance of practice effects in experimental design.
:::

## Statistical Test: Learning Effect

Is there a significant improvement from Trial 1 to Trial 5?

```{webr-r}
# Paired t-test: Trial 1 vs Trial 5
trial1 <- reflex |> pull(t1)
trial5 <- reflex |> pull(t5)

t.test(trial1, trial5, paired = TRUE)
```

## Individual Differences

Let's look at each participant's trajectory:

```{webr-r}
ggplot(reflex_long, aes(x = trial, y = distance_cm,
                         color = id, group = id)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_color_viridis_d(option = "plasma") +
  labs(
    x = "Trial",
    y = "Distance (cm)",
    title = "Individual Learning Curves",
    color = "Participant"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(color = "#275882", face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "right"
  )
```

## Bonus: Reaction Time Distribution

What's the distribution of reaction times (in ms)?

```{webr-r}
ggplot(reflex_long, aes(x = rt_ms)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 10, fill = "#3498db", color = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean(reflex_long$rt_ms),
             linetype = "dashed", color = "#e74c3c", linewidth = 1) +
  annotate("text", x = mean(reflex_long$rt_ms) + 5, y = 8,
           label = paste0("Mean: ", round(mean(reflex_long$rt_ms)), "ms"),
           hjust = 0, color = "#e74c3c", fontface = "bold") +
  labs(
    x = "Reaction Time (ms)",
    y = "Count",
    title = "Reaction Time Distribution"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(color = "#275882", face = "bold")
  )
```

**Typical human reaction time**: 150-300 ms for visual stimuli

---

::: {.key-finding}
#### Summary

Participants showed a clear **learning effect** over 5 trials, with reaction times improving significantly from Trial 1 to Trial 5. The average reaction time (~175ms) is within the expected range for visual-motor tasks.
:::
